prose:
Lighthouse Park is a 75-hectare patch of old-growth coastal forest at the tip of West Vancouver, with granite rocks running down to the ocean and the Point Atkinson lighthouse, which has guided ships since the 1870s. For engagement and proposal photos it gives you two very different looks in one walk: tall, mossy forest and wide-open sea.

I'm Joenell, a Vancouver engagement and proposal photographer. This guide covers the best viewpoints, when to go, parking, and the permit rules that are easy to miss.

The Best Viewpoints for Photos

Juniper Point

At the park's northwest corner, looking out to Passage Island, Bowen Island and Howe Sound. Reached on the Juniper Loop trail from the far end of the parking lot. A strong sunset spot.

Shore Pine Point

West of the lighthouse, with views over Howe Sound, the Strait of Georgia and the Gulf Islands. Follow the Shore Pine Trail west and look for the sign.

West Beach

Looks back at the lighthouse across the water, which makes it the classic "lighthouse in the background" spot.

Eagle Point and Starboat Cove

On the east side, facing Burrard Inlet, Vancouver and the Lions Gate Bridge. Eagle Point is quieter; Starboat Cove is about a 10-minute walk east of the lighthouse and has a small beach with an old boat.

The forest trails

Between the viewpoints, the trails run under huge Douglas firs and cedars. The light there is soft and even, which is perfect for relaxed walking photos, even on a cloudy day.

When to Go

  • Golden hour: the west-facing points (Juniper and Shore Pine) catch the sunset over the water.
  • Cloudy days: the forest is at its best in soft, grey light.
  • Weekdays: much quieter than weekends, and easier for parking.
  • Hours: the park is open daily from 7 am to 10 pm.

See also the best time of year for engagement photos in Vancouver.

For a Surprise Proposal

The rocky points are natural stages with the ocean behind you, and a sunset walk is an easy cover story. Smaller points like Juniper Point are calmer than the main lighthouse viewpoint. I arrive first, wait like any other visitor, and we agree on a signal before you kneel. More in my Vancouver surprise proposal guide, or see a real proposal at Bowen Lookout on Cypress Mountain.

Permits and Rules

  • Ceremonies: West Vancouver's wedding permit lists Lighthouse Park as not available. For a ceremony nearby, Whytecliff Park is one of the District's bookable wedding locations.
  • Photo sessions: the District's $145 non-exclusive permit covers ceremonies and photo sessions in its parks, and Lighthouse Park isn't on that permit's list. I check with the District for your date before we plan a session there.
  • No setup: no arches, chairs, décor or music.
  • The lighthouse grounds are a national historic site and aren't open to the public; the views are from the surrounding rocks and viewpoints.

Parking and Practical Tips

  • Getting there: from Marine Drive, turn onto Beacon Lane toward Horseshoe Bay and follow the signs.
  • Parking: pay parking year-round; the lot is small, fills quickly in good weather and closes when full.
  • Washrooms: outhouses near the Juniper Loop entrance and along Beacon Lane Trail.
  • Shoes: the trails have roots and rocks. Wear good shoes and change for photos at the viewpoint.
  • Outfits: soft colours stand out well against the green forest and blue water. See what to wear for engagement photos.

Pricing

Engagement sessions are $225 (up to 60 minutes, at least 30 edited images) and surprise proposals are $250 (up to 45 minutes, at least 20 edited images). Lighthouse Park is within my usual area, with no travel charge. More in the complete Vancouver engagement photos guide and on the pricing page.
